skill.name: senior-secops
skill.description: SecOps reference skill with basic Python scripts for project checks, vulnerability review, and compliance reporting. It includes supporting guidance documents.
skill.summary: Run basic SecOps checks and review security guidance for a project.
skill.author: davila7

security_audit.summary: Most command-related static findings are false positives caused by Markdown code fences and documentation references, not Ruby backtick execution. The three Python scripts do perform user-directed output file writes, which can overwrite paths chosen with --output. No prompt injection, data exfiltration intent, or hidden network behavior was found in the reviewed files.

remediation.issue: Unrestricted report output path in CLI scripts.
remediation.suggestion: Write reports under a dedicated output directory, or warn before overwriting an existing file.

remediation.issue: Environment setup command may overwrite an existing .env file.
remediation.suggestion: Use a non-overwriting copy step, or ask users to check for an existing .env file first.

remediation.issue: Command examples include broad development and deployment commands.
remediation.suggestion: Label examples as optional and add safety notes for production-affecting commands.

content.value_statement: Security teams need fast project checks without building a workflow from scratch. This skill provides basic scripts and reference guidance for SecOps review.
actual_capabilities: Provides three Python CLI scripts for security scanning, vulnerability assessment, and compliance checks.
Validates a target path before running each script.
Prints a simple report with target, status, and finding count.
Can write JSON results to a user-selected output file.
Includes reference documents for standards, vulnerability workflows, and compliance topics.
limitations: The included scripts are basic templates and do not perform deep security analysis.
The documentation contains generic guidance that needs project-specific review.
The scripts do not enforce safe output paths or overwrite protection.
It does not replace professional penetration testing or compliance certification.

use_cases.title: Project Security Snapshot
use_cases.description: Run the provided scanner against a repository and summarize the basic report for initial triage.

use_cases.title: Compliance Preparation
use_cases.description: Review compliance guidance and collect a simple status report before a formal audit.

use_cases.title: Developer Security Review
use_cases.description: Use the reference files to guide secure development checks during a feature review.

prompt_templates.title: Run a Basic Scan
prompt_templates.prompt: Use senior-secops to review the current project. Run the appropriate scanner, summarize results, and list clear next steps.

prompt_templates.title: Check Compliance Readiness
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the compliance checker and reference guide to assess this project. Identify missing evidence and practical remediation tasks.

prompt_templates.title: Triage Vulnerability Work
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the vulnerability assessor guidance to organize open security issues by risk, ownership, and recommended response.

prompt_templates.title: Design a SecOps Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Combine the scripts and reference documents into a repeatable SecOps workflow for this repository and team.

output_examples.input: A user asks for a security scan of a repository.
output_examples.output: A concise report showing the target path, completion status, finding count, and recommended follow-up actions.

output_examples.input: A team asks whether a project is ready for a compliance review.
output_examples.output: A readiness summary with missing evidence, security control gaps, and prioritized remediation tasks.

output_examples.input: An engineering lead asks for a vulnerability triage plan.
output_examples.output: A prioritized plan that groups issues by risk, owner, response timing, and validation needs.

best_practices: Run the scripts on a reviewed project path and inspect generated files before sharing results.
Treat the reference documents as starting points and map them to your actual controls.
Keep security findings tied to evidence, owners, and clear remediation dates.
anti_patterns: Do not treat the template scripts as a complete vulnerability scanner.
Do not write output files over important project files.
Do not apply deployment commands from examples without environment review.

faq.question: Does this skill perform a full penetration test?
faq.answer: No. It provides basic scripts and guidance for initial SecOps review.

faq.question: Can it create reports?
faq.answer: Yes. The scripts can print reports and optionally write JSON output files.

faq.question: Is it suitable for compliance certification?
faq.answer: No. It can help prepare evidence, but certification requires formal review.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Does it send data to external services?
faq.answer: No evidence found in the reviewed files for network transmission or external data sharing.

faq.question: What should users verify before running it?
faq.answer: Users should verify the target path, output path, and any commands that affect deployment.
